validity.researcher_notes:
TOOLING NOTE: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every live WebFetch this session, matching the scope note that wiki_citations.json is empty for the whole batch. I recovered the wiki page's actual reference list anyway via the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org snapshot 20260520035334 of https://www.gem.wiki/Dandot-Gali_Jagir-Wah_Gas_Pipeline_II), which is permitted under the 'read gem.wiki for leads, never cite it' rule -- I use it only to find what GEM's own citation actually is, not as a citation itself.

What that archived wiki page cites for Length/Diameter/Status/Owner (footnote [1]) is: SNGPL's own 'Transmission System' article page (article.jsp?pgids=461&pgname=Transmission%20System&secs=ss3146974axd5872&cats=ct96563iok34952&artcl=artuyh8erf285294&artids=341). I independently rediscovered this same URL via a plain web search (DuckDuckGo HTML) for 'Dandot Gali Jagir Wah gas pipeline SNGPL', which returned it as a live, indexed SNGPL page -- i.e. two independent paths converged on the same source, and it is NOT a dead/rotted citation as I initially suspected from the generic-looking landing pages other pgids variants of this URL return.

I fetched this exact URL live today (2026-08-07, HTTP 200, verified via url_verifier.py) and it renders SNGPL's full transmission-pipeline inventory table (a numbered list of every named line segment with diameter-in and length-km columns). The current live table (row numbers 148-150) reads verbatim: '148 DANDOT - GALI JAGIR - WAH 10 87.7 / 149 DANDOT - GALI JAGIR - WAH 16 153.51 / 150 DANDOT - GALI JAGIR - WAH 30 64.22'. This is SNGPL's own primary asset register, not a GEM-derived or third-party page.

EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, strongly. The pipeline is a real, currently-listed SNGPL transmission asset, independently and directly named on SNGPL's own live technical inventory (not merely mentioned in passing -- the row literally reads 'DANDOT - GALI JAGIR - WAH').

SPEC: GEM's Length (151.92km) = exactly 87.7 + 64.22, i.e. the sum of the SNGPL table's 10in and 30in rows for this corridor. GEM's Diameter ('10, 30' in) = exactly the two diameters of those same two rows. This is not a coincidental match -- it is precise to two decimal places on the length. So the number GEM is carrying is directly and correctly traceable to the primary source, just aggregated across two of the source's three line items (see the modeling-choice caveat in 'recommendation' above).

Second, independent corroboration (not cited as a [ref] URL, but genuine corroboration): this batch's own GulfPub (Petroleum Economist PE World Map, source_tier=2, scraped 2025-12-11, staged at batches/pakistan-gas/staging/recon-gulfpub-20260807/canonical_records.json) contains SIX separate records on this same corridor with diameters 10in (x3: 'Dhulian - Gali Jagir' x2 + 'Gali Jagir - Wah'), 16in (x2: 'Gali Jagir Line II' + 'Gali Jagir - Wah'), and 30in (x1: 'Gali Jagir Line', CC1->Gali Jagir, 125.529km/78mi, 900 MMcf/d) -- all attributed to operator/owner 'Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd', matching GEM's Owner1 exactly. GulfPub independently confirms the same three-diameter (10/16/30in) structure on the same named corridor that SNGPL's table shows, from a wholly separate scrape origin. I am NOT citing GulfPub as a proposed_ref -- its own recorded source_url field is just SNGPL's generic homepage (https://www.sngpl.com.pk), which url_verifier confirms does NOT contain 'Gali Jagir', so citing it would be a fabricated-looking reference. GulfPub's individual segment lengths (e.g. 30in CC1->Gali Jagir = 125.5km) don't reconcile cleanly against SNGPL's 64.22km 30in row -- plausibly a different start-point convention (CC1, a compressor station, vs. Dandot) rather than a data conflict, and I'm not treating it as a spec disagreement given SNGPL's table is the primary source and matches GEM exactly.

DUPLICATE check vs the 63-pipeline roster: NOT a duplicate of P4161 ('Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah Gas Pipeline I', 16in, 153.51km). P4161 corresponds to the SNGPL table's separate 16in/153.51km row; P4162 corresponds to the 10in/87.7km + 30in/64.22km rows. These are three distinct diameter classes in the primary source, consistent with the roster's other Roman-numeral loopline families (Sui-Multan Gas Pipeline/Loopline I/II/III; Sidhnai-Faisalabad Gas Pipeline/II; Faisalabad-Shahdara Gas Pipeline-I/II) where 'I'/'II' denote genuinely separate parallel pipes on one named corridor, not double-counted segments.

CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is directly supported -- this line item sits on SNGPL's own 'Transmission System' inventory page, not a distribution/gathering list. Fuel=Gas is uncontested (SNGPL is a gas transmission/distribution utility; the page is explicitly about its gas transmission network).

ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) 100% is directly supported -- the asset is listed on SNGPL's own corporate transmission-system page, and GulfPub's independent scrape lists the same operator/owner for every matching segment on this corridor. StartLocation=Dandot (Chakwal, Punjab) / EndLocation=Wah (Punjab) match the source row name 'DANDOT - GALI JAGIR - WAH' directly. One minor open point I could not resolve with available tooling: GEM's EndPrefecture/District for Wah is blank, and the archived gem.wiki page's prose describes Wah as being 'in Rawalpindi, Punjab' -- Wah Cantonment is colloquially associated with both Attock and Rawalpindi districts depending on the source/era; I did not have a citable primary source to adjudicate this and did not want to fabricate a district value, so I am leaving it as an unresolved minor note rather than proposing a fill.

STATUS: Operating is supported -- the segment appears on SNGPL's current, live transmission-system inventory (fetched today), which by definition lists in-service assets; GulfPub's matching records also carry status_raw='Operating'.

Net: existence, classification, attribution, and duplicate-check all hold up on strong, independent, primary-source evidence (SNGPL's own live asset register, reinforced by GulfPub's independent scrape). Length and Diameter are traceable exactly to two of the source table's three line items for this corridor -- a caveat about how GEM's two-entity model divides the source's three rows is noted for awareness, not flagged as an error, since the recorded numbers are precisely correct for the aggregation GEM chose. Capacity remains blank; GulfPub shows capacity figures for related segments (300/900/10000 MMcf/d) but these are inconsistent in scale across near-duplicate GulfPub records (one 10000 MMcf/d figure looks like a scrape/placeholder artifact) and none is a citable public URL, so per instructions I am leaving Capacity blank rather than force a number.
